page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.large is an entry-level memory-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The server is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Cache structures include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance includes no local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote disk options, and features a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight the limited raw compute throughput inherent to a single physical core. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 981.0 and a multi-core score of 1184.0. PassMark results show a CPU score of 1820.12, an extended instruction score of 1444.67, and a database operation score of 570.26. Large block uncached memory throughput reached 10.42 GB/sec for reads and 9.25 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused tests, the instance executed 1.44 million Redis SET operations per second and handled 1.75 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the ecs.r5.large centers on its high memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside low multi-threaded compute capability. From a resource perspective, it avoids over-provisioning compute when memory footprint is the primary bottleneck. This hardware profile suits in-memory caching layers such as Redis, lightweight relational databases, and background services that require 16 GB of working memory without demanding intensive CPU cycles.
